Zach Nunn calls for action on insider trading and housing reform in recent posts
I. S. Corley
U.S. Rep. Zach Nunn, who represents Iowa's Third Congressional District, used his social media platform to highlight issues ranging from congressional stock trading to housing policy and legislative transparency.
On July 21, 2026, Nunn posted: "Some are calling it the fastest one minute in @the535news history."
The following day, he addressed concerns over financial conflicts of interest among lawmakers, stating on July 22, "$200 million: That’s how much Members of Congress made last year from trading stocks while overseeing the industries behind the stock tickers. The Stop Insider Trading Act is a must-pass bill to restore trust in Washington by holding lawmakers who use their position for profit".
Later that day, Nunn turned attention to housing policy and institutional investment in real estate. On July 22, he wrote: "Who should get the keys: Wall Street or Iowa families? A starter home was meant for the young couple in Winterset, not hedge fund managers in New York. Our housing law puts Iowa families in the driver's seat and holds institutional investors accountable, with penalties up to $1".
Nunn's statements reflect his focus on government accountability and economic policy. His office is based in Des Moines and serves residents across 21 counties within Iowa's Third Congressional District (official website). He has prioritized bipartisan efforts aimed at strengthening the economy, supporting agriculture, ensuring accountability, enhancing national security, and aiding families. As a member of both the House Financial Services Committee and House Agriculture Committee, Nunn has been active on issues related to financial oversight and rural interests.
His office also provides constituent assistance with federal agencies, further reflecting his commitment to serving central and southern Iowa.
